title: fix(sinker): Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn take a start and an exit pick
body:
## What changed

- The Sinker Burn takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `PickCapability::Ring`: the ring is its orbit.
  - A pick is an angle round the burn position (`x`, `y`). The start pick is where the orbit starts. The exit pick is where the orbit ends.
  - Circular: the circle starts at the start angle and makes one full turn counter-clockwise. With an exit pick it continues to the exit angle.
  - Planetary: the spiral turns from the start angle and reaches the radius there. The closing circle starts there.
  - Vector: the vector toward the start pick is burned first. The vector toward the exit pick is burned last.
  - After the exit angle the electrode feeds back to the burn position and retracts up the burn axis, as before.
- The Sinker Side Burn takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `PickCapability::Ends`.
  - The side move has two ends: the burn position and the wall end (the burn position moved by `amount` toward the wall).
  - A pick on the wall side of the middle of the move chooses the wall end. A pick on the other side chooses the burn position.
  - The start pick chooses the end where the electrode plunges. The exit pick chooses the end where it retracts.
- These picks are refused by name, at the command door and at generation. No pick is moved.
  - A pick on a Sinker Burn without an orbit: `Sinker Burn: a start point is not taken without an orbit - a straight plunge starts and ends at the burn position; ...`.
  - A pick on the burn position: it gives the orbit no angle.
  - A pick between two vectors of a vector orbit: `... is on no vector of the orbit ...`.
  - An exit vector that the vector order cannot end on.
  - A side burn pick at the middle of the side move: it chooses no end.
- With no pick each generator calls the earlier function. Each path without a pick is byte-identical.
- A path with a pick has one more note. The note names the start point and the exit point.
- The Geometry tab of each kind has a "Start point" group and an "Exit point" group with typed X and Y rows. A Sinker Burn without an orbit shows "Not taken - a straight plunge starts and ends at the burn position; state an orbit on the Passes tab".
- The schema text of MCP `edit_operation` names the two kinds. `list_operation_types` answers `start_exit: { start: true, exit: true, field: "picks" }` for them.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn. The door refused each pick. `sinker_orbit::orbit_offsets` always started the orbit at +X. `sinker_side::side_burn_worn` always plunged and retracted at the burn position.

## Design

The issue is exact about what each pick sets. Where it is silent, I took the smallest change. The decision file is `docs/decisions/3333-sinker-start-exit.md`.

- **The laws hold at each angle.** A circle keeps its own vertices, and the start and the exit are added vertices. The four axis directions stay vertices, so the walls move out by exactly the radius. Each vertex is on or inside the radius (`sinker_orbit::on_disc`). The undersize law and the cavity limits (`cavity_x`, `cavity_y`) count the radius, so they hold. A vector orbit keeps its directions; a pick changes the order only.
- **The orbit returns to the burn position before the retract.** The layered burn plunges each layer on the burn axis, so the orbit must end there between two layers. The retract law is not changed. The issue says "where the orbit ends before the retract": the last position on the radius is the exit angle.
- **The side burn's ends.** The issue says "the side where the side move begins". I read "side" as an end of the move. The `direction` parameter stays the one input for the wall. The electrode is at the same two positions at the same tip for each choice, so the burned volume is the same. `side_burn_worn` runs first, so the allowance law, the wear law and the layer law refuse before a pick is read.
- **No new field.** The picked generators take the ends as an argument: `sinker_wear::burn_compensated_between` and `sinker_picks::side_burn_between`. `SinkerParams` and `Orbit` are not changed.
- **No new command and no new file key.** The picks use the existing `EditOperationParams` and the `picks` field of #3339. The stamp already includes the picks.
- The new code is in one motion module, `crates/motion/src/sinker_picks.rs`. The UI rows are in one new file, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/sinker_pick_rows.rs`.

## Tests

Pins in the `start_exit_shared` suite of `camcraft-app` (`crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared/sinker.rs` and `sinker_side.rs`). Each name below has the prefix `sinker::`. The first seven were red before the fix, on unchanged `upstream/main` code at `707dac12a`. No new test binary is added.

- `a_circular_orbit_starts_at_the_start_pick_and_ends_at_the_exit_pick` (also: no gouge in `simulate_document`; a start at +X gives the automatic moves; undo and redo restore the previous path)
- `a_planetary_orbit_reaches_its_radius_at_the_start_pick`
- `a_vector_orbit_starts_on_the_picked_vector_and_ends_on_the_exit_vector`
- `a_pick_that_the_orbit_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
- `side::a_side_burn_starts_and_ends_at_the_picked_ends_of_its_side_move` (five choices of ends; the wall position in the stock sim; no gouge; undo and redo restore the previous path)
- `side::a_side_burn_pick_at_the_middle_of_the_move_is_refused_by_name`
- `side::mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_sinker_picks_and_refuses_an_impossible_one_by_name`
- `side::the_generator_refuses_an_impossible_sinker_pick_by_name` (added with the fix; it calls `operation::generate` directly)
- `a_picked_orbit_keeps_the_undersize_law_and_the_cavity_limits` (added with the fix; a rough pass with a pick generates inside the radius, and an orbit past the cavity is refused by the undersize law)

More tests:

- `camcraft-motion` lib: `sinker_picks::tests::*` (7 tests: the automatic orbit is unchanged; each picked orbit stays inside its radius and keeps the axis vertices and each circle vertex; the vector order; the refusals; a layered worn burn; the side ends; the side burn keeps each refusal).
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::sinker_pick_rows::tests::*` (3 tests: labels, switches, the seeded draft, the "Not taken" line).

Red before the fix: the pins that existed then (the first six of the list, and after it the MCP pin) failed with `Sinker Burn: a start point is not taken - the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships; clear it on this operation` (or the same text for `Sinker Side Burn`).

Mutation results (old code back, pins run, fix restored):

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| `pick_kinds.rs` from `upstream/main` | the first seven app pins (all that set a pick through the command door) |
| `pick_kinds.rs`: the door check of the two kinds removed | `a_pick_that_the_orbit_cannot_hold_...`, `side::a_side_burn_pick_at_the_middle_...`, `side::mcp_edit_operation_sets_...` |
| `sinker_op.rs` from `upstream/main` | the circular, planetary and vector pins, `side::the_generator_refuses_...` |
| `sinker_side_op.rs` from `upstream/main` | `side::a_side_burn_starts_and_ends_...`, `side::the_generator_refuses_...` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "no orbit" guard off | `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_reads_angles_and_refuses_by_name` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "on the burn position" guard off | `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_reads_angles_and_refuses_by_name` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "on no vector" guard off | `sinker_picks_a_vector_orbit_keeps_its_directions_in_the_picked_order`, `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_...` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the exit order guard off | `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_reads_angles_and_refuses_by_name` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "middle of the side move" guard off | `sinker_picks_side_ends_choose_the_nearer_end_and_refuse_the_middle` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the circle makes half a turn | `sinker_picks_every_picked_orbit_stays_inside_its_radius_and_keeps_the_axis_vertices` |

All pins are green with the fix restored. The mutations ran on the same source code, before the pins moved into the `start_exit_shared` suite and before the ninth pin was added. The ninth pin was not in a mutation run.

Expected-change test: `start_exit_shared::every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` pinned "only the contour and the wire take a pick". It now names Sinker Burn as `Ring` and Sinker Side Burn as `Ends`.

## Review fixes

The latest review requested two merge conflict fixes. The held local merge includes upstream main `10ea81a2a1da2f883d43385757db802e83c99fd1`. It was not pushed because the heavy gate failed. The remote head remains `c2f1d36cdbd3e73da4327508cc9fe8e071e194a7`.

- `operation/pick_kinds.rs` keeps the sinker orbit and side-move refusal arms. It also keeps main's wire exit refusal arm.
- `mcp/tools.rs` keeps the wire start and exit description. It also keeps the sinker orbit and side-move descriptions.
- `the_mcp_doors_name_the_pick_fields_and_the_kinds_that_take_them` now checks both families' schema descriptions.
- The existing sinker and wire MCP pins check each family's command refusal behavior.

Verification target: held local merge tested `a9bc76c8a3db5b3d1c13787171819eaec61233e9`, against current upstream main `10ea81a2a1da2f883d43385757db802e83c99fd1`.

| Check | Result on held local merge |
|---|---|
| `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_SWEEP=off CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | GREEN: 61 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 5.8 min; 2,957 passed, 37 ignored |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | RED: 108 steps, 1 unexpected failure, 0 stalled; 37.9 min. Four configured known-fail probes were red as expected and counted as OK. Heavy catalog: 4 passed. |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | GREEN: 36.68 s |
| `app suites: example_catalog` and reached golden suites | GREEN: catalog 43 passed, 4 ignored; adaptive 1 passed; edge work 1 passed; sinker burn 15, orbit 7, side 6, undersize 10, wear 6 passed |

The first quick run encountered missing dependency artifacts (`E0463`). A local clean of the affected packages and a run with the compile cache disabled resolved the build failure. The successful quick run on the held local merge used the environment values shown above.

The heavy gate failed in `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`, at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:80`. The test expected a mesh with 6,228 triangles and got 5,232. The conflict fix remains local because this gate is red. No extra code fix is permitted in this review round. The warm worktree `.claude/worktrees/fix-3980` remains in place.

Review-round mutation proof:

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Remove both sinker refusal arms | `sinker::side::mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_sinker_picks_and_refuses_an_impossible_one_by_name` | Expected RED: an invalid burn-position pick was accepted |
| Remove the wire refusal arm | `edit_operation_sets_the_wire_exit_pick_and_refuses_one_it_cannot_hold` | Expected RED: the generic taper refusal replaced the expected exit refusal |
| Use the `HEAD^1` schema description, without the wire exit meaning | `the_mcp_doors_name_the_pick_fields_and_the_kinds_that_take_them` | Expected RED: the wire exit description was missing |
| Remove the sinker schema descriptions | `the_mcp_doors_name_the_pick_fields_and_the_kinds_that_take_them` | Expected RED: the sinker descriptions were missing |

All four mutations failed as expected. After the fixes were restored, `start_exit_shared` passed all 13 tests and `mcp_wire_contour` passed all 9 tests.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff upstream/main -- '*.nc' '*.cl' examples/catalog` is empty. The catalog and all reached golden suites ran and passed, as listed above. No golden was regenerated for the conflict resolutions.

## Not exercised

- The heavy gate ran on the held local merge and failed as stated above. The earlier implementation round ran only the light lane.
- A posted NC program with a pick was not made. The post reads the explicit CL moves, and the pins assert those moves.
- The viewport does not pick these points. The rows are typed, or MCP sets the picks.
- A real EDM control did not run these paths. The fixtures are synthetic.
- The picks were not tested with a cavity outline (#1810) or with a finish pass. A rough pass is pinned. The undersize law counts the orbit radius only, and the motion test asserts that no picked vertex leaves the radius.

## Screenshots

The Geometry tab of the operation page. "Before" is `upstream/main`: the two groups say "Not taken". The images are on the fork's images-only branch `pr-screenshots`, at commit `ddb2e0528`.

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sinker Burn without an orbit | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ddb2e0528029f5b88af1f77a5b6349695d32e0c4/pr-3980/sinker-burn-no-orbit-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ddb2e0528029f5b88af1f77a5b6349695d32e0c4/pr-3980/sinker-burn-no-orbit-after.png) |
| Sinker Burn with a circular orbit, the two groups switched on | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ddb2e0528029f5b88af1f77a5b6349695d32e0c4/pr-3980/sinker-burn-orbit-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ddb2e0528029f5b88af1f77a5b6349695d32e0c4/pr-3980/sinker-burn-orbit-after.png) |
| Sinker Side Burn, the two groups switched on | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ddb2e0528029f5b88af1f77a5b6349695d32e0c4/pr-3980/sinker-side-burn-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ddb2e0528029f5b88af1f77a5b6349695d32e0c4/pr-3980/sinker-side-burn-after.png) |

## Overlaps

- #3957 (Wire Contour exit pick) and #3970 (Drill, Bore, Thread hole order) change the same shared hook: the arms of `KindInfo::pick()` and the last lines of `OpParams::pick_refusal` in `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`, the pick sentence of `s_edit_op` in `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, and the capability test in `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared.rs`. #3970 also adds a call at the same place in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/op_page.rs`. Each PR adds its own arms. The PR that merges second refreshes from `main`. This PR is not stacked: the three PRs are parallel slices of #1448.
- #3963 touches `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` in a different function.
- #3674 touches `crates/app/src/lib.rs` in a different line.

Effort: high

Changelog: Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn take a start point and an exit point: the angle at which the orbit starts and ends, and the end of the side move where the electrode plunges and retracts. An impossible point is refused by name.

Fixes #3333
